_risk_note: P2. Test substrate only, no product code and no migration. acquireChatDefinerLock (packages/db/src/test-harness.ts) runs `new pg.Client` then connect() then `SELECT pg_advisory_lock($1)` with no try spanning them, and end() is reachable ONLY through the returned release(). A rejection from connect() or from the lock query therefore leaves a client the caller cannot close, because the caller never received the handle that closes it. The cost is concrete rather than theoretical: setupNonSuperuserOwnerContext assigns chatDefinerLockRelease from THIS return value, so a throw here leaves it null and leaves its own teardown() with nothing to release.

verification._note: Two runtime constraints are encoded here deliberately, both learned the expensive way by earlier lanes. (1) The gate's subprocess inherits NOTHING from an interactive shell, so DATABASE_URL and DATABASE_URL_TEST are inline rather than assumed exported. (2) No entry may contain an angle bracket: autopilot-review-readiness.mjs treats one as an unresolved placeholder and halts CONTRACT_INVALID, which rejects even an ordinary 2-to-1 redirect. Entry 2 is a scope-containment PROPERTY measured against the pinned base, not a pinned count of anything that moves. The db suite runs under the repo's own vitest.config.ts, whose fileParallelism is true — that is the condition under which a leaked lock client actually costs something, so it is the condition the fix is verified under.
